document_class: 3. Fee schedule and maker/taker structure
title: Trading Fees [Kalshi Exchange Fee Schedule]
document_date_note: no publication date is printed on the document; the only date it states is the effective date below
attribution_label: as stated in Kalshi's published fee schedule

clauses.quote: Trading fees are only charged for orders that are immediately matched with orders sitting on the orderbook. Trading fees are not charged for orders placed that are not immediately matched and are instead left as resting orders on the orderbook unless they are included in our "Maker Fees" section.
clauses.what_it_constrains: Which side of a fill bears the trading fee, and therefore whether the passive leg of any two-leg strategy is costed at all.

clauses.quote: fees = round up(M x 0.07 x C x P x (1-P))
clauses.what_it_constrains: The taker fee function. Fee is a function of price, so cost is not constant across the price range and is maximal near P=0.5.

clauses.quote: M = the multiplier for each contract (default is 1 unless otherwise indicated)
clauses.what_it_constrains: Taker fee is per-series: the multiplier is set per contract series, so a fee computed for one series does not transfer to another.

clauses.quote: fees = round up(M x 0.0175 x C x P x (1-P))
clauses.what_it_constrains: The maker fee function. Where the maker multiplier is non-zero Kalshi charges makers a positive fee - it is not a rebate.

clauses.quote: M = the multiplier for each contract (default is 0 unless otherwise indicated)
clauses.what_it_constrains: Default maker multiplier is zero, so whether a resting order is charged at all is a per-series fact that must be read off the non-standard-fee table, never assumed.

clauses.quote: round up = rounds up such that the fee + positionCost is rounded to a centicent
clauses.what_it_constrains: Fee rounding is always upward; small-size strategies pay a rounding premium that does not vanish as size falls.

clauses.quote: Maker fees are charged for orders placed that are not immediately matched and are instead left as resting orders on the orderbook. These fees are only charged when a trade is ultimately executed, there are no fees associated with canceling a resting order.
clauses.what_it_constrains: Quote-and-cancel activity is not itself fee-bearing; cost accrues only on execution.

clauses.quote: There is no settlement fee.
clauses.what_it_constrains: Holding to expiry incurs no additional exchange fee under this schedule.

clauses.quote: There is no membership fee.
clauses.what_it_constrains: No fixed access cost is imposed by this schedule (bears on document class 4, membership limits).

clauses.quote: Users accessing Kalshi via a third-party Futures Commission Merchant may be charged fees by their Futures Commission Merchant that vary from the above fee schedule.
clauses.what_it_constrains: The schedule binds only direct access; an intermediated participant's cost is not determined by this document.

clauses.quote: Please refer to https://kalshi.com/fee-schedule for scheduled upcoming fee changes.
clauses.what_it_constrains: The document is not self-sufficient over time: pending changes live at a separate URL, which this arm retrieved (KS-VR-Q18) and found client-rendered with no fee text in the bytes.

tables_not_quoted: The document also carries a general per-price fee table, a per-series non-standard maker/taker multiplier table (roughly 90 series), and two tiered perpetual-futures fee tables (a taker schedule and a maker schedule across 11 volume tiers). document_class: 1. Rulebook and its amendments (member-facing contract of adhesion)
title: Kalshi Member Agreement
document_date_note: NO date is stated anywhere in the retrieved text. Recorded as absent, never estimated.
attribution_label: as stated in the Kalshi Member Agreement

clauses.quote: You acknowledge that Kalshi's Rulebook allows Kalshi to implement market maker programs. Kalshi believes that these programs will promote liquidity and orderliness on the Kalshi Exchange. Under the rules, market makers will make markets on Kalshi in exchange for receiving benefits. The benefits can include monetary benefits, such as discounts on fees, rebates on fees, revenue share from fees, and other monetary benefits. Market makers who receive these benefits may be able to price their quotes in ways that are materially different from other Kalshi members who are not eligible to receive these financial benefits. Market makers may also be eligible for sophisticated risk management tools, such as order protections whereby orders are canceled if the market maker's trading session disconnects from the Exchange, and may be eligible to greater throughput to the Exchange. These risk management tools enable market makers to effectively manage the risks of their market making activity, and may not be available to members who are not market makers. These tools may give market makers a trading advantage over members who are not market makers; and
clauses.what_it_constrains: DECISIVE for any quoting or latency-sensitive strategy run by a non-market-maker. The venue states in its own member agreement that market makers may receive fee discounts, fee rebates, fee revenue share, disconnect-cancel protection and GREATER THROUGHPUT, none of which are available to ordinary members. A cost or fill-rate figure built from the public fee schedule and the public rate-limit tiers is therefore an upper bound on a non-market-maker's competitiveness against the members who set the quotes.

clauses.quote: You further acknowledge that market makers may be required, during specific times, to maintain a maximum spread size and may be required to maintain a minimum depth within the spread. Outside of the required times, market makers are not required to, and potentially will not, maintain the maximum spread size and minimum depth. Therefore, pricing and liquidity outside of the required times may be worse than during the required times.
clauses.what_it_constrains: Liquidity is contractually guaranteed only inside windows the document does not identify. Any strategy whose fills depend on a resting two-sided book must treat depth as time-varying by design, not as a stationary property.

clauses.quote: This Agreement may be amended unilaterally by Kalshi upon notice to You. You will be deemed to agree to each such amendment if You do not terminate this Agreement prior to the effective date of the amendment;
clauses.what_it_constrains: Access terms are unilaterally amendable; no version of the executability preconditions is contractually stable for a participant.

document_class: 6. API documentation and rate limits
title: Rate Limits and Tiers
attribution_label: as stated in Kalshi's published developer documentation

clauses.quote: Every authenticated request costs **tokens**. Your tier sets your **budget**: the rate, in tokens per second, at which your balance refills. Your sustained rate for an endpoint is `budget ÷ cost`.
clauses.what_it_constrains: Throughput is metered as a token bucket, not as a fixed request count. Any claim about achievable order rate must name a tier.

clauses.quote: Most requests cost the default of **10 tokens**.
clauses.what_it_constrains: Converts a tier's token budget into a sustained order rate: Basic write budget 100 tokens/s equals 10 orders/s; Prestige write budget 8,000 tokens/s equals 800 orders/s.

clauses.quote: | **Write** | Order placement, amends, cancels, order groups, the RFQ quote flow, and block trade proposal accepts. |
clauses.what_it_constrains: Order traffic draws on a budget separate from market-data reads; a strategy is not throttled by its own polling.

clauses.quote:
* **Basic**: complete account signup.
* **Advanced**: call the [Upgrade Account API Usage Level endpoint](/api-reference/account/upgrade-account-api-usage-level).
* **Expert, Premier, Paragon, Prime, and Prestige**: earned automatically from your trading volume (see [Earning higher tiers](#earning-higher-tiers-by-volume) below), or assigned by Kalshi.
clauses.what_it_constrains: DECISIVE eligibility gate. The two highest-throughput tiers cannot be bought or requested: they are earned from realised volume share or granted at the venue's discretion. A new participant starts at Basic (write budget 100 tokens/s = 10 orders/s at default cost), so any strategy specified at high order rates is not executable at entry.

clauses.quote: `volume share = your trailing 30-day volume ÷ (previous month's exchange volume × 2)`
clauses.what_it_constrains: The tier ladder is relative to total exchange volume, so the throughput available to a participant is a function of the rest of the market, not of the participant alone.
The exact volume-share thresholds for each throughput tier, and the hysteresis between earning and keeping one.

clauses.quote: A batch request costs the same as making each call individually. Every item in the batch is billed separately
clauses.what_it_constrains: Batching does not relax the throughput ceiling; a multi-leg strategy cannot use batch submission to evade its tier budget.

clauses.quote: The whole batch must fit in the bucket at once. A 25-order create batch needs 250 tokens available when it arrives, or the entire batch is rejected.
clauses.what_it_constrains: All-or-nothing batch admission: a multi-leg order set can be rejected in full on a token shortfall, which is a leg-risk source for any simultaneous multi-leg strategy.

clauses.quote: 429 responses do not currently include `Retry-After` or `X-RateLimit-*` headers.
clauses.what_it_constrains: A throttled client is given no scheduling information; backoff must be inferred, which is itself a latency cost.

document_class: 3. Fee schedule and maker/taker structure
title: Fee Rounding
attribution_label: as stated in Kalshi's published developer documentation

clauses.quote:
* Direct member balances are aligned to `$0.0001` (`0.01c`)
* Non-direct member balances are aligned to `$0.01` (`1c`)
clauses.what_it_constrains: Balance precision differs by membership class, so the same fill returns a different net amount to a direct member than to an FCM-intermediated one.

clauses.quote: When a trade produces a balance change that is more precise than the user's target balance precision, the exchange charges a **rounding fee** to bring the balance back to that target.
clauses.what_it_constrains: A cost component over and above the published fee formula, unmodelled by the fee schedule, and larger in relative terms for a non-direct member.

clauses.quote: **Net fee** = trade fee + rounding fee - rebate (always >= \$0.00)
clauses.what_it_constrains: Net fee is floored at zero: no fill returns a net credit to the participant under this mechanism.

clauses.quote: The fee accumulator is maintained per order across all fills regardless of whether the fills are taker or maker. If an order initially takes (matching resting orders) and then becomes a resting maker order, the accumulated rounding carries over to subsequent maker fills.
clauses.what_it_constrains: Per-fill cost is path-dependent within an order, so a strategy's realised cost cannot be computed fill-by-fill in isolation.

The two are not expressed in comparable units, and which side binds a simultaneous two-venue strategy depends on the Kalshi tier the participant actually holds - which per ks-vr-d06 clause d06-c4 is earned from volume share or granted at the venue's discretion, not chosen. clauses.quote: During periods of increased latency, Polymarket US applies a **5-second stopgap** to inbound orders. If an order has been received by Polymarket US but has not been processed within 5 seconds, we reject it to protect you from a bad fill at a stale price.
clauses.what_it_constrains: Orders are silently dropped under latency. A two-leg cross-venue strategy can have one leg fill and the other rejected precisely when the venues are moving - leg risk is concentrated in exactly the states where a discrepancy would appear.
